title: AST Failure To Salvage Moose: Farewell GMU 19C [AK25091599]
summary: On 09/08/2025, McGrath AWT contacted two hunters with a dead 52" bull moose at the Farewell Strip. Investigation determined Jeffery Harris, age 42 of Anchorage, took the moose on the evening of September 5th. The moose was left in the field for approximately 14 hours before being field dressed. Temperatures throughout the region were warm and wet. The meat of the moose spoiled due to not being properly cared for in a timely manner. Investigation also determined Harris took the two front shoulders, and other chunks of meat, and discarded them in the brush due to their putrid smell and colors. Harris was issued a citation for failing to salvage all edible meat. The moose rack and rotten meat were seized as evidence. Arraignment was set for October 9, 2025, in the Aniak Court.

summary: Alaska State Troopers, in coordination with the Alaska Mountain Rescue Group (AMRG), successfully rescued a hiker in distress near the Indian Creek Trailhead late Saturday night. The rescue operation proceeded despite a brief cancellation of the SOS call, as the hiker later reported he couldn't feel his feet. After midnight, the Alaska Mountain Rescue Group was deployed to the last known coordinates. At approximately 2:55 AM, rescuers made contact with the hiker about a mile from the parking lot

title: AST Wildlife Violation: Petersville [AK24057910]
summary: On June 16, 2024, at approximately 1208 hours, the Alaska Wildlife Troopers found two cell cameras overlooking a bear bait station off Petersville Rd. While checking the cameras it was discovered that they were activated and that there was cellular coverage in that area. The cameras were seized as evidence and search warrants were done on them. The evidence gathered from the warrants revealed that Dominic Nickles was receiving photographs from the cameras, which assisted in the harvest of a bear. Also, that Kenneth Ess took a black bear while knowing that the camera was actively sending pictures of the bait sight. Both Nickles and Ess received citations for using cameras that can send wireless communications to take a bear.

title: AST Homicide Investigation: Sutton [AK25028413]
summary: On March 27, 2025, at around 8:25 pm, the Alaska State Troopers responded to the Sutton area to conduct a welfare check. Responding Troopers located 56-year-old Sutton resident Nicholas Wells, deceased from multiple gunshot wounds. title: AST Taking deer closed season: Prince of Wales Island [AK20028661]
summary: On 4/27/20, Alaska Wildlife Troopers on Prince of Wales Island were notified of several deer that had been taken illegally during the closed season. AWT responded to the area and located four gut-piles, each with an unborn fawn, as well as, the heads and lower legs of four adult female deer. The deer appeared to have been recently killed (within the past 12 hours). The deer had likely been shot elsewhere and then transported to the remote log landing on Saltery Point near Hydaburg, where they were gutted and processed. Several items of evidence were located at the scene, and the investigation is ongoing. Anyone with information about this incident is encouraged to contact the Alaska Wildlife Troopers-Prince of Wales post at 907-826-2291.
